equation: Fresnel normal-incidence transmissivity T_sol = 4 n1 n2 / ((n1+n2)^2 + kappa^2)
note: standard; correct form for a lossless incident medium

equation: Beer-Lambert I(z) = I0 exp(-alpha z), alpha = 2 omega kappa / c
Skin depth delta = 1/alpha = c / (2 omega kappa)

note: standard; inside the target medium n2, not n1, applies

equation: Induced potential Delta V = P_LF d / (eps0 eps_LF)
Delta V = [2 chi2 T_sol exp(-alpha z) d / (n1 c eps0 eps_LF)] I_peak
I_peak,min >= [n1 c eps0 eps_LF / (2 chi2 T_sol exp(-alpha z) d)] V_th
I_peak,min >= [n1 c eps0 eps_LF (n1+n2)^2 / (8 n1 n2 chi2 d)] exp(2 omega kappa z / c) V_th
note: consistent; drops the kappa^2 of T_sol (kappa ~ 0.5 for water at 1 THz: ~4% effect)

equation: 'HWI Standard Equation' I_peak,min >= (1/D) [2 n2 c eps0 eps_LF / (chi2 d)] [((n1+n2)^2 + kappa^2) / (2 omega kappa)] ln(I0/I_target) V_th
note: INCONSISTENT: the right side has units of intensity x time (J m^-2). ln(I0/I_t)/(2 omega kappa) = z/c, so the exponential depth factor of p. 37 became a linear one; the Fresnel factor also differs from p. 37

equation: Thermal time tau_th = rho C_p w^2 / (4 k)
